clue.text: Small, mean house, something for one's digs

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a hovel is a squalid, wretched dwelling

explanation.surface: An estate agent's sneer at a poky home that is only fit for lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digs' looks like lodgings, as the house in the surface suggests, but here it means digging holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A spade-like tool is what a person uses for digging, so it is an implement for their digs.

clue.text: The wrong direction to capital in a state

indicators.note: wrong suggests the word The has its letters put in the wrong order

parts.note: travel towards London is traditionally said to be going up to town

explanation.surface: A complaint that someone set off the wrong way to the state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a state is an idiom for being agitated and flustered, which is what this phrase means.

clue.text: House and grounds, or ground

parts.note: a villa is a large country or suburban house
a park is the grounds of a country estate

explanation.surface: An estate agent listing a property as house plus grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: VILLA PARK is the football ground of Aston Villa in Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a particular football stadium, so it is an example of a sports ground.

clue.text: Childishly left tree in such a state?

definitions.meaning: a child might wrongly form the past tense of leave with a regular ending
a tree in leaf is said to be covered with foliage

explanation.surface: A child abandoning a tree, perhaps in some condition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a child's wrong past tense of the verb meaning to go away and an adjective meaning having foliage.

clue.text: Depressed by defeat in game, does she share with you?

parts.note: flat means low in spirits
mate is checkmate, the winning move in chess

explanation.surface: Someone low after losing a game, and a question about who lives with you.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rents a home together with you is someone sharing your accommodation.

clue.text: Quarter-size feature of space-time

parts.note: a fourth is one quarter of a whole
dimension means measurement or extent

explanation.surface: A physicist describing something a quarter of the size within space-time.
explanation.definitionFit: In relativity, time is treated as an additional coordinate alongside the three of space.

clue.text: Prayer woman raised to maiden' with song

indicators.note: in a down entry, raised means the name is written upwards, back to front

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
an aria is an operatic solo song

explanation.surface: A woman lifting a prayer to a maiden in song.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin devotion addressed to the Virgin is a well-known Catholic prayer, also set to music.

clue.text: Extra large fungus

parts.note: more means additional or extra
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A description of an extra large mushroom.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an edible mushroom with a honeycomb cap, a prized kind of fungus.

clue.text: Old city cat, one of twelve in the pound

definitions.text: one of twelve in the pound

parts.note: Troy is the ancient city of Homer's Iliad
the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: An ancient city's cat, one of a dozen in the animal pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The troy pound used for precious metals is divided into twelve of these weight units.

clue.text: Enjoying oneself as long as one likes?

definitions.meaning: read literally, being at one's pleasure is having fun
a phrase meaning at one's own discretion or whim

explanation.surface: Having a good time for as long as you please.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at one's discretion, as one wishes, and can be read literally as being in enjoyment.

clue.text: Sound scheme to make jumpers

indicators.note: sound tells us to take the word as it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a ruse is a crafty scheme or trick

explanation.surface: A sound plan for knitting sweaters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumpers' suggests sweaters, a British word for them, but here they are kangaroos.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos, known by this short Australian name, move by leaping, so they are jumpers.

clue.text: Back father and mother perhaps, as such an heir

indicators.note: back tells us to write the short word for father the other way round

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a mother is an example of a parent

explanation.surface: Supporting both parents, as a dutiful heir would.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir apparent is one whose right to inherit cannot be displaced, the standard collocation.

clue.text: A Dubliner, full of colour

parts.note: Leopold Bloom is the Dublin hero of Joyce's Ulysses

explanation.surface: A colourful character from Ireland's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants in flower are bright with blossom, so the word describes something full of colour.

clue.text: No exploiter of animals can shortly become a star

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a vegan uses no animal products at all

explanation.surface: An animal-rights activist who can soon become a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the last letter of VEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, so it is an example of a star.

clue.text: Partner no longer using drug: criticise, but not blame

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
on means taking a drug, as in on heroin
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
to rate can mean to scold severely

explanation.surface: A former partner off drugs, deserving criticism but not blame.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE in the sense of berate is an old use.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of an accusation is to find them free of fault, i.e. not to blame them.

clue.text: So wet, swimming around end of pier

indicators.note: around says the swimming word is placed so it surrounds the other letter

parts.note: dipping means taking a quick swim

indicators.note: end of tells us to take the final letter of pier

explanation.surface: A swimmer soaked after a dip near the end of a pier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soaked through, with water falling from it in drops, is extremely wet.

clue.text: Taking a hand in forecasting, friend's vague, about right

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: about says the vague word goes round the letter for right

parts.note: misty means hazy or unclear

explanation.surface: A friend lending a hand with a forecast, though rather vague about it.
explanation.definitionFit: This art foretells the future by reading the lines of a person's hand.

clue.text: Drive me into Surrey, towards my place

indicators.note: drive means push in, so the word me is driven into another
into says where the small word is pushed

parts.note: Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, was a Tudor poet

explanation.surface: A request for a lift into the county of Surrey, back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surrey' looks like the English county south of London, but it is the title of the poet Henry Howard.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading for home means going in the direction of where the speaker lives.

clue.text: As keen reader, beam to receive new work

indicators.note: to receive says the beam word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a boom is a long spar or beam, as on a sailing boat

indicators.note: new says the letters of work are made fresh by rearrangement

explanation.surface: A keen reader beaming at being given a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like a verb, to smile broadly, but it is a noun, the spar; 'new' gives KWOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loves reading and always has their nose in a book is called this, after the larva that eats paper.

clue.text: Ship about to become a national symbol

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: keel is a poetic word for a ship

explanation.surface: A ship on the point of being adopted as a nation's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The keel is the ship's backbone; the word stands for the whole ship. The answer is the emblem of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is worn on St David's Day as an emblem of Wales, a national symbol.

clue.text: Conscript Nemo, could it be?

parts.note: taking an omen as a sign and turning it upwards, as a down entry reads, gives the letters of Nemo

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether Captain Nemo could be called up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as instructions: a SIGN is an omen, and UP in a down entry writes it backwards, giving NEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist, or to enrol someone for service, is a phrasal verb close to conscripting.

clue.text: Copper for one said to show resilience

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: copper is an example of a metal

explanation.surface: A policeman said to show toughness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, a British slang word, but here it is the element.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit and courage in the face of difficulty is resilience, the sense of this word.

clue.text: One from Argentina has uniform to follow

definitions.meaning: the ballroom dance that originated in Buenos Aires
in the NATO phonetic alphabet T is followed by U, which is Uniform

explanation.surface: An Argentine with a uniform following him.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance came from Argentina, and the same word is the radio code for T, just before Uniform.

clue.text: Best sleep cut short, party being at this extreme?

parts.note: number one, written NO I, means the best

indicators.note: cut short tells us to drop the last letter of the sleep word

parts.note: a siesta is an afternoon sleep

explanation.surface: A best night's sleep interrupted by a party at its peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' drops the A from SIESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A party at its loudest extreme makes more din than at any other time.

clue.text: Sinful animal?

parts.note: the name of a slow tree-dwelling mammal is also one of the seven deadly sins, laziness

explanation.surface: A beast that is wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the slow South American mammal and the deadly sin of idleness.

clue.text: One used to pop

definitions.meaning: a person manipulated by others, like the humblest chess piece
pop is slang for leaving goods at a pawnbroker's for a loan

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person exploited as a tool and to pledge goods for a loan.

clue.text: Brecht's effect appears something deceptive to people

parts.note: a lie is something meant to deceive
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A playwright's theatrical effect seeming to deceive the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Brecht's Verfremdungseffekt, distancing the audience from the drama, is usually translated with this word.

clue.text: Obliged to take role in Salinger adaptation?

parts.note: to be someone is to play that part
Holden Caulfield is the hero of Salinger's The Catcher in the Rye

explanation.surface: An actor bound to accept a part in a film of a Salinger novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'be Holden': to play Holden Caulfield in a screen version.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in someone's debt or under an obligation to them is the meaning of this word.

clue.text: Spy's extraordinary revolutionary spirit

indicators.note: extraordinary says the letters of Spy are arranged out of the ordinary

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: A spy's remarkable revolutionary zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' shuffles SPY into PSY; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word for soul or mind is used in English for the human spirit.
